answer: Since the cedar index is rebuilt each epoch, the walnut audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, since the wander embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 79% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
